rows.title: Spam’s $3.50 ‘affordable protein’ price tag has Hormel Foods’ CEO feeling good about the future in the age of the cash-strapped consumer
rows.standfirst: Jim Snee, CEO of Hormel Foods, isn’t worried about weight-loss drugs like Ozempic, either.

rows.title: Millennials and Gen Z face ‘snowballing and snowballing’ debt as high card balances and interest rates eat into their credit scores
rows.standfirst: “If left unaddressed, the issue compounds very, very quickly.”

rows.title: European inflation has now fallen from its 10.6% peak after the Russian invasion of Ukraine to just 2.6%
rows.standfirst: Prices spiked after Russia cut off most supplies of natural gas to Europe, sending energy prices through the roof.

rows.title: Philadelphia’s famously rowdy sports fans claim another victim: One of the best hot dog deals ever. Inflation is no match for a Phillies fan
rows.standfirst: “It wasn’t just the throwing,” Philadelphia Phillies official John Weber told the AP. “But obviously, you know, the throwing was a little bit of a tipping point.”

rows.title: The Fed is just not going to cut interest rates this year, top economist Torsten Slok says
rows.standfirst: “The bottom line is that the Fed will spend most of 2024 fighting inflation,” Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok wrote in a Friday note to clients.

rows.title: A new kind of remote work city just drove a $2 trillion gain in the housing market. ‘Pricey metros and pandemic boomtowns’ are drifting, Redfin finds
rows.standfirst: The national housing market is now worth $47.5 trillion, after a 5.3% increase over the last year, per a Redfin analysis of over 90 million homes.

rows.title: Buying a house has gotten so expensive that homebuyers need to make about $50,000 more than they did pre-pandemic to afford one
rows.standfirst: Housing affordability ‘feels the most intense’ it has in 20 years, real estate brokerage owner says

rows.title: Swiss voters back boosting pensions—something they hadn’t done in 176 years—as high cost of living takes toll
rows.standfirst: The government-orchestrated rescue of Credit Suisse last year may have favored the result: “People have been angry.”

rows.title: A judge struck down Chicago’s ‘mansion tax’ but it’s still on the Super Tuesday ballot. Here’s what’s at stake
rows.standfirst: The referendum asks Chicago voters to support an increase on a transfer tax for properties over $1 million. It’s a one-time buyer’s fee.

rows.title: Miami-Dade is the latest county to go into debt to try to do what its private sector won’t: Build houses
rows.standfirst: Miami-Dade county is short more than 90,000 affordable homes.

rows.title: Commercial real estate tycoon says the industry is entering its final stage of grief: Acceptance
rows.standfirst: RXR CEO Scott Rechler says his peers must accept the “regime change” in commercial real estate after decades of low rates.

rows.title: Blame Hawaii bureaucrats for the high cost of housing, local professors find in economic study
rows.standfirst: The median price of a new two-bedroom condo in Hawaii is $672,000, more than twice the nationwide average of $300,000.

rows.title: Top economist who called the 2008 housing crash pours cold water on soft landing, pointing to rate hikes and a softening labor market
rows.standfirst: “We Americans tend to be perennial optimists,” Gary Shilling said during an interview on “The Retirement Lifestyle Advocates.”

rows.title: Texas’s big 3 housing markets built 300% more homes than California’s—despite having a far smaller population
rows.standfirst: “If a developer sees an opportunity, or sees a need to build more homes, it’s a lot easier to get that done when the government isn’t telling you no,” Zonda’s chief economist, Ali Wolf, told Fortune.

rows.title: Top economist Gary Shilling predicts a ‘considerable revival’ in housing activity—but it’s going to take 3 or 4 years to unfreeze the housing market
rows.standfirst: The “lock-in effect” pushes a housing market recovery to years away.

rows.title: The U.S. housing market is headed into a pivotal spring season as home sellers wait for their sweet spot, according to Opendoor
rows.standfirst: Opendoor’s December survey saw an 18% increase in the number of homeowners ready to sell in the next year–a higher proportion than in any quarter.

rows.title: Jerome Powell is walking on eggshells when it comes to interest rates, saying cuts are ‘likely’ but warning he can’t do anything ‘too soon’
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve chair’s interest rate indecision continues as the market watches—and wonders.

rows.title: The Pandemic Housing Boom drove a $91,000 windfall for the average U.S. senior
rows.standfirst: That was the median increase in net worth between 2019 and 2022 for households headed by someone age 65 or older, per research from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

rows.title: Roughly $30 billion could be slashed from real estate agents’ commissions: Fed economists pose solution to the ‘anomaly’ in the American housing market
rows.standfirst: Richmond Fed economists suggest an “à la carte” model for real estate commissions, arguing it could redistribute buyer agents’ profits to the tune of billions of dollars.

rows.title: Hospital monopolies are buying up independent physicians and hiking prices–but Congress has an opportunity to rein them in
rows.standfirst: They change the sign on the door, then offer the same health care services at the same location, but charge more.

rows.title: The remote-work revolution means only managers can afford to live in pricey cities
rows.standfirst: Pricier home values in cities are linked to a higher concentration of managers, according to new research from ADP.

rows.title: Europe is losing hope of a spring rate cut even with inflation far off peak
rows.standfirst: There likely won’t be an interest rate cut at the European Central Bank’s meeting Thursday.

rows.title: Broke boomers are moving in with their millennial kids, who are seething
rows.standfirst: As more boomers reach retirement age, many are facing the stark reality of insufficient savings—and turning to their adult children for support.

rows.title: Real-estate billionaire Barry Sternlicht offers a solution to the U.S. inflation problem: ‘Tell Congress to stop spending money like drunken sailors’
rows.standfirst: Starwood Capital cofounder and CEO Barry Sternlicht says aggressive federal spending is hindering the Fed’s goal to tame inflation.

rows.title: The housing market’s deep freeze is showing signs of thawing
rows.standfirst: Low inventory and high housing costs were two major challenges last year—but more supply is entering the market.

rows.title: Housing inflation data mystery deepens as government says email to ‘super users’ was a ‘mistake’
rows.standfirst: Jeffrey Hill, associate commissioner at the BLS, said an employee “blind-copied a number of requesters and referred to them as super users — this was a mistake.”

rows.title: British retail mogul takes a 30% loss on his London mansion as city’s richest home sellers watch house prices tumble
rows.standfirst: Bobby Arora sold a townhouse in the exclusive Belgravia district for £23.5 million ($30 million) – it was bought by Arora for £34 million about a decade ago.

rows.title: Baby boomers aren’t going to crash the housing market—they’re powering it
rows.standfirst: Fears of a “silver tsunami” are overblown, John Burns Research and Consulting’s vice president of demographics tells Fortune.

rows.title: Jerome Powell says ‘the housing market is in a very challenging situation right now’ and interest rate cuts alone won’t solve a long-running inventory crisis
rows.standfirst: Even once the current problems dissipate, the Fed chair said, “we’ll still be left with a housing market nationally, where there is a housing shortage.”

rows.title: ‘We need more homes in general’: Biden administration says housing crisis can’t be corrected until we build a lot more
rows.standfirst: President Biden will call on Congress for resources to ‘build more housing’ amid the U.S. supply crunch, deputy Treasury secretary Wally Adeyemo tells Fortune.

rows.title: Data shows Gen Zers are finally ready to spend more–but it’s getting harder to sell them anything
rows.standfirst: For most consumers, word of mouth remains the primary driver of purchasing decisions.

rows.title: Americans have never been more concerned about their finances. But that doesn’t mean they plan to cut back
rows.standfirst: “Financial shock fatigue” is holding people back.

rows.title: Welcome to the housing election: Americans are trapped in their houses or outside the market looking in, and it’s focusing their thinking for November
rows.standfirst: “While the economy is strong on paper, a lot of families aren’t feeling the benefits, because they’re struggling to afford the house they want or already live in.”

rows.title: ‘Dr. Doom’ economist warns Trump reelection is ‘greatest threat’ to face global markets right now
rows.standfirst: A combination of punitive import tariffs and more tax cuts could potentially spark an investor revolt and lead to the next financial crisis.

rows.title: JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon: Not out of the woods on recession, but ‘worst case would be stagflation’
rows.standfirst: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warns that the prospect of a recession isn’t outside the realm of possibility.

rows.title: Multibillion-dollar Bud Light maker and Coca-Cola bottler publicly shamed for waiting months to pay U.K. suppliers
rows.standfirst: Report says hundreds of thousands of small business are at risk of insolvency because of slow paying practices by big companies.

rows.title: Inflation has battered the toy market—but defiant Lego saw sales climb 4% in 2023: ‘We continue to grow’
rows.standfirst: Lego’s sales grew even as the toy industry is at its worst in “more than 15 years,” CEO Niels Christiansen said.

rows.title: One of the few forecasters to predict violence and chaos in 2020 thinks spiraling inequality is pushing the U.S. closer to collapse than Russia
rows.standfirst: Academic Peter Turchin blamed spiraling inequality in the West for increasing the chances of total anarchy.

rows.title: Inflation rose for a second straight month, endangering prospect of Fed rate cuts this summer
rows.standfirst: Consumer prices in the United States picked up in February for the second month running—a bad sign for Biden’s reelection prospects and any rate cuts.

rows.title: Airbnb bans all indoor security cameras to ‘prioritize the privacy of our community’
rows.standfirst: The majority of listings, the company says, did not report having a security camera on premises.

rows.title: Vinyl records are making their comeback as one of Britain’s inflation metrics for the first time in 30 years—and of course, you can thank Taylor Swift
rows.standfirst: Vinyl’s comeback reflects “a resurgence in popularity,” according to ONS, as the records surge to new highs in sales.

rows.title: Inflation is now ‘moving more sideways than down’—and it could keep the Fed from cutting rates anytime soon
rows.standfirst: Rent, gas prices drive up headline number, but investors still hopeful for interest-rate relief starting in June.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon says the Fed should hold off on cutting interest rates because the economy is ‘kind of booming’
rows.standfirst: Dimon said there’s a roughly 35% chance of a U.S. soft landing, but stagflation and recession remain a threat.

rows.title: Shrinkflation is coming for your home
rows.standfirst: The median new-home size is the smallest it’s been in more than a decade.

rows.title: Jerome Powell just revealed a hidden reason why inflation is staying high: The economy is increasingly uninsurable
rows.standfirst: Housing and auto insurance costs are soaring because of climate change and more expensive car parts, says Fed Chairman Jerome Powell.

rows.title: U.K. rebounds with 0.2% GDP growth in January, now on track to exit recession
rows.standfirst: Data next week is expected to show a sharp slowdown in inflation, and investors are betting the Bank of England will begin cutting rates in August from their highest level in 16 years.

rows.title: We analyzed 46 years of consumer sentiment data–and found that today’s ‘vibecession’ is just men starting to feel as bad about the economy as women historically have
rows.standfirst: The overall vibes hit their nadir in June 2022–the month of highest inflation and the lowest level of consumer sentiment ever recorded for men.

rows.title: $22 trillion worth of the housing market—or 44% of all homes in the U.S.—is at risk of severe or extreme damage from environmental threats
rows.standfirst: “Climate risk is a big deal,” says Realtor.com economist Jiayi Xu, adding that “people are tolerating these risks in exchange for more affordable housing.”

rows.title: Joe Biden is admitting that nobody wants to sell their house—and it’s offering an incentive to fix it
rows.standfirst: The Pandemic Housing Boom increased the price of starter homes a whopping 45%. The White House thinks a $10,000 tax credit will get the market moving.

rows.title: Snacking is king—and inflation-proof—as Gen Zers and millennials resort to small indulgences even with tight wallets, Toblerone and Cadbury maker finds
rows.standfirst: Gen Z and millennials don’t care as much for the regimented three-meals as they turn to snacks through the day as small doses of pleasure.

rows.title: The housing market’s pivotal spring selling season is more like a shopping window: A trickle of new listings collides with sky-high prices and mortgage rates
rows.standfirst: New listings aren’t enough to bring all would-be homebuyers off the sidelines, because affordability doesn’t seem to be improving meaningfully.

rows.title: The uninsurable housing market: 26% of homeowners worry climate change will put them underwater either literally or figuratively
rows.standfirst: Homeowners insurance premiums are up 300% in California since before the pandemic, insurance exec says.

rows.title: The economy was just hit with a one-two punch of bad data
rows.standfirst: In the fight between the mighty American consumer and the always lurking recession, it hasn’t been much of a contest—until now?

rows.title: ‘It’s a freaking nightmare right now’: Housing affordability crisis decades in the making explodes during election year
rows.standfirst: America has failed to build enough homes for its growing population, striking at the heart of the American dream of homeownership.

rows.title: Your Zara and Stradivarius shipments might be delayed as the Red Sea crisis presses on
rows.standfirst: Inditex warned that costs may rise from rerouting ships due to Houthi rebels’ attacks as it makes a killing in its retail business.

rows.title: 40-year-old homeowner says economy doesn’t add up: ‘I’m making the most money I’ve ever made, and I’m still living paycheck to paycheck’
rows.standfirst: “There’s this wild disconnect between what people are experiencing and what economists are experiencing,” says Nikki Cimino, a recruiter in Denver.

rows.title: Why don’t we trust funeral directors? Transparency and innovation can redefine the industry–if the FTC allows it
rows.standfirst: More consumers are comparing their options when they shop for funerals–but only 18% of funeral homes post pricing online.

rows.title: Dollar Tree is more like $7 Tree as value chain lifts its price ceiling
rows.standfirst: The discount chain said over 300 items will see price points from $1.50 to $7 this year as part of its “multi-price expansion strategy.”

rows.title: The $1.8 billion ‘conspiracy’ verdict that rocked the real-estate industry has turned into a groundbreaking $418 million settlement
rows.standfirst: Realtors just reached a settlement that will reshape their industry after a historic antitrust judgment—and you should expect lower commissions and fewer real estate agents.

rows.title: Homeowners are red, renters are blue: The broken housing market is merging with America’s polarized political culture
rows.standfirst: “Across the age spectrum, at every point, owners are substantially further to the right than renters,” says Aziz Sunderji, a former analyst who explores housing data on his substack.

rows.title: A wealthy Bay Area enclave formed a ‘heritage alliance’ to become a historic district—and it all started after a new family bought a home in the neighborhood
rows.standfirst: The initiative metastasized into what appears to be an effort to skirt state housing laws altogether.

rows.title: The huge $418 million realtor settlement means you can find a home online without having to pay a buyer’s agent commission
rows.standfirst: As part of the settlement, the NAR won’t require a broker advertising a home for sale to offer upfront compensation to a buyer’s agent.

rows.title: Germany faces a recession, and an economic recovery ‘isn’t yet in sight’ according to Economy Ministry
rows.standfirst: Due to weakened domestic demand, high financing costs and the subdued sentiment among private households and companies.

rows.title: Top real-estate CEO sees decades of housing pain ahead: ‘What the Fed did will have a 30-year tail on it’
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve’s interest rate hikes will be felt across the housing market for decades, Redfin CEO Glenn Kelman said.

rows.title: FOMO-driven buyers could jump at Nvidia’s ‘three day AI lovefest’—but Fed Chair Powell is ready to play the spoiler, Ed Yardeni says
rows.standfirst: “Bearish traders might take the market down Tuesday afternoon,” veteran economist and market watcher Ed Yardeni warns.

rows.title: The Goldman economist who predicted the financial crash and soft landing says AI will be good for the U.S. economy but will ‘destroy employment in some areas’
rows.standfirst: But AI’s boost to productivity will ripple across the country and lift GDP growth, Goldman’s chief economist predicts.

rows.title: The incredible surge in home prices is set to continue in Southern metros, a new projection says—here’s why housing market inflation will just keep running
rows.standfirst: Home price appreciation superiority comes down to stronger employment growth and affordability, according to Capital Economics.

rows.title: Housing is so unaffordable in major cities that millennials are moving back to the suburbs, Harvard study finds
rows.standfirst: Millennials are leading a “back to the city” reversal.

rows.title: Food prices cool in the U.K. as inflation slips 3.4% in February, way below expectations
rows.standfirst: “Inflation is heading in the right direction and should fall below the Bank of England’s 2% target sometime in the Spring,” said a lead economist at the CBI.

rows.title: Fannie Mae CEO, who’s responsible for 1 in 4 U.S. mortgages, says she learned to be a ‘risk manager’ from Jamie Dimon
rows.standfirst: Priscilla Almodovar oversees $4.3 trillion in mortgage assets.

rows.title: Can Bidenomics beat inflation? One skeptical Pennsylvania factory town highlights another election challenge
rows.standfirst: “I can tell you it’s going to be a hard-fought battle for both Trump and Biden,” says Rayni Taylor, a union steel worker, adding that “a lot of the common folk” are downbeat on the economy.

rows.title: Fannie Mae’s CEO says the housing market hasn’t killed the American Dream yet. Buying a home ‘might just take a little longer’
rows.standfirst: To Americans struggling to buy, Priscilla Almodovar says: “Being a renter is fine.”

rows.title: Seattle mother lives with her husband, 2 young kids in a 180-square-foot ‘micro-apartment’ that costs only $900 a month
rows.standfirst: “It’s warm. We can cook ourselves. We have a private bathroom. It’s quiet,” says Barbara Peraza-Garcia, whose family fled crime in Venezuela.

rows.title: U.K. retailer Next, owner of Reiss and Fat Face, beats expectations as it posts record profits. ‘We are now entering a new era’ says CEO Simon Wolfson
rows.standfirst: Next expects profit to expand to nearly $1.3 billion this year as rising wages free up British shoppers to spend more on fashion.

rows.title: Bundesbank president hits back at recession-plagued Germany’s ‘sick man of Europe’ title: ‘I’m more worried that Europe is getting sick’
rows.standfirst: Germany is being tarred with a sickly moniker as the country tries to turn around its flatlining economy.

rows.title: ‘Greedflation and shrinkflation’ are front and center in the Pennsylvania Senate race
rows.standfirst: Democratic Sen. Bob Casey, seeking a fourth term, is outraged by price increases. His opponent, former hedge fund CEO David McCormick, doesn’t buy it.

rows.title: Gold prices hit a record high above $2,200 after the Fed’s dovish press conference
rows.standfirst: Gold prices have surged 10% since mid-February and 20% since their October lows, but its move upward is about a lot more than interest rates.

rows.title: ‘The American Dream is still very much alive,’ Fannie Mae CEO insists—and she has essential advice for first-time homebuyers
rows.standfirst: “Did my parents dream of having a home? Was that home what changed the trajectory of our life? Absolutely,” said Fannie Mae CEO Priscilla Almodovar.

rows.title: Turkey’s inflation problem is so severe the central bank just hiked interest rates to 50%, months after it said it was done raising rates
rows.standfirst: “The decision to respond so quickly…is clearly a very encouraging signal for the policy shift and should help to maintain investor confidence,” Capital Economics’ Liam Perch wrote in a Thursday note.

rows.title: Former broker unimpressed by $418 million NAR settlement—says they couldn’t agree on lunch let alone a conspiracy
rows.standfirst: Assoc. dean Ken Johnson, whose research focuses on real estate economics, still expects sellers’ agents and buyers’ agents to split home-sales commissions, or share them.

rows.title: Easter is around the corner—but the real hunt for Brits this year will be to find cheap chocolate eggs amid eye-watering inflation as high as 62.5%
rows.standfirst: It’ll cost to have a sweet tooth this Easter. Which? analysis points to a 12.6% chocolate inflation at U.K. supermarkets compared to last year.

rows.title: The housing market is so bad this Long Island house has no running water or power—and it’s on sale for $500,000
rows.standfirst: Off-the-grid housing options are gaining popularity—but some of them are still really pricey.

rows.title: Olive Garden’s earnings just pulled back the curtain on the economy: The rich are dining out while the poor are falling back
rows.standfirst: “We’re clearly seeing consumer behavior shifts,” Darden CEO Rick Cardenas said on an earnings call. “At every brand, transactions fell from incomes below $50,000.”

rows.title: JPMorgan’s head of research says immigration is undeniably a ‘good thing’ for the economy, as the bank forecasts even higher US GDP growth this year
rows.standfirst: Immigration has helped fill job openings during a time of low unemployment and kept consumer spending high, according to JPMorgan’s Joyce Chang.

rows.title: Housing market data suggests the most optimistic buyers during the pandemic are more likely to stop paying their mortgages
rows.standfirst: The wave of optimistic homebuyers in 2021 and the first half of 2022 are particularly vulnerable to drops in price expectations.

rows.title: ‘I don’t want to pay a buyer’s agent’—homeowners are charged up after $418 million settlement, top real estate CEO says
rows.standfirst: Redfin’s chief executive says the firm is getting “more aggressive” on selling homes directly to consumers following the settlement.

rows.title: Real-estate agents are going extinct just like travel agents did, award-winning professor says. ‘You just don’t need’ them anymore because of the internet
rows.standfirst: Home buyers and sellers are no longer “dependent” on real estate agents, Andrew Spieler of Hofstra University tells Fortune.

rows.title: Remote workers say they’d return to the office if they get housing benefits—and many would even take those over a pay raise
rows.standfirst: Some would even give up three weeks of vacation for some extra help with their mortgage, a new report finds.

rows.title: Homebuyers expecting big savings after realtor settlement likely in for letdown: ‘Everyone is turning this ruling into what they want it to be’
rows.standfirst: “I expect most of the gain to be captured by the seller, so the impact on home prices will be small,” said Moody’s Analytics Chief Economist Mark Zandi.

rows.title: Homes in England are more cramped than ones in New York City and offer the worst value for money in the developed world
rows.standfirst: With 38 square meters on average per person, London homes are even more cramped than those in New York City.

rows.title: Legoland will toy with ‘surge pricing’ this summer to hike ticket rates—but only on sunny days
rows.standfirst: Legoland, London Eye and Madame Tussaudes operator says dynamic pricing could help “avoid overcrowding” and offer more flexibility.

rows.title: NYC vacancy rates are so low—and affordable housing is so sparse—that a super PAC has formed to elect politicians to build more homes
rows.standfirst: New York City vacancy rates hit a historic low in February.

rows.title: Tricky local regulation and a decade of cheap money in the housing market has created a ‘perfect storm’ for prices to stay high, top real-estate CEO says
rows.standfirst: “Unbelievable demand has sort of been the story of the last five to seven years, and that’s due to really the villain being supply,” Invitation Homes’ CEO Dallas Tanner said.

rows.title: Atlanta Fed president Raphael Bostic says he only expects one rate cut this year
rows.standfirst: Bostic goes against Wall Street and the Fed’s consensus view, which predicts three rate cuts in 2024.

rows.title: Nearly half of all investors expect a ‘no landing’ scenario for the economy where inflation remains but there’s no recession, Deutsche Bank survey shows
rows.standfirst: “You could say [it’s] an implied Goldilocks ‘no landing’ for now…the markets quite liking their porridge on the warmer side,” Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid wrote.

rows.title: There’s one week in April that will be the best time to sell a house this year, Realtor.com says. Here’s why
rows.standfirst: “The week of April 14–20 is expected to have the ideal balance of housing market conditions that favor home sellers, more so than any other week in the year,” Realtor.com’s economic research analyst said in a report.

rows.title: Trader Joe’s increases the price of bananas for the first time in over 20 years
rows.standfirst: The 21% increase is the end of an era.

rows.title: The housing market is so unaffordable that buyers need to make $30,000 more than they currently do to buy a home
rows.standfirst: But that’s an improvement from last year when they needed to close a more than $40,000 shortfall, according to a new Redfin analysis.

rows.title: Renting will be cheaper than buying for years, especially as home prices keep setting new all-time highs
rows.standfirst: Home prices and rents are high, but the latter “will remain by far the most cost-effective option” until the end of 2026, Capital Economics predicts.

rows.title: Larry Fink joins Jamie Dimon and Jerome Powell in sounding the alarm on ‘snowballing’ national debt: ‘The situation is more urgent than I can ever remember’
rows.standfirst: Rising fiscal deficits have fuelled America’s gravity-defying economic growth, but bond investors may revolt, plunging the country into a decade of austerity.

rows.title: It’s a ‘nepo’ housing market. More than a third of Gen Zers and millennials expect their parents to help with a down payment, survey finds
rows.standfirst: “Because housing costs have soared so much, many young adults with family money get help from Mom and Dad,” Redfin’s chief economist, Daryl Fairweather, said.

rows.title: Home Depot’s largest acquisition ever is an $18.25 billion bet on the housing market’s severe shortage of new homes
rows.standfirst: The acquisition target, SRS Distribution, provides materials for professionals like roofers, landscapers and pool contractors.

rows.title: The U.S. economy just won’t quit — fourth-quarter GDP was revised even higher than initial estimate
rows.standfirst: The government upped its estimate of GDP growth for the last quarter of 2023 to 3.4%, from an earlier 3.2%.

rows.title: America’s best-known gas analyst decries ‘misinformation from politicians.’ The president is basically ‘powerless’ to control the price at the pump
rows.standfirst: “At the end of the day, one president in one country in a world with 200-some countries is rather powerless to control the price of a global commodity,” GasBuddy’s Patrick De Haan said.

rows.title: Self-made real estate millionaire Barbara Corcoran says home prices could go up another 10% if mortgage rates drop
rows.standfirst: “If rates go down just another percentage point,” the “Shark Tank” star said, “prices are going to go through the roof.”

rows.title: A $2.3 million home listing in Nantucket slashed its price by a whopping 74% after its shoreline experienced drastic erosion in just a few weeks
rows.standfirst: Small vacation towns are reeling at the effects of climate change.

rows.title: Virginia governor vetoes bill that would have boosted minimum wage from $12 to $15 over two years, saying it wasn’t needed
rows.standfirst: Republican Gov. Glenn Youngkin also vetoed a bill that would have allowed for recreational retail sales of marijuana.

rows.title: $50,000 of public money was misused to build secret apartments inside Bay Area train stations, authorities say
rows.standfirst: San Mateo prosecutors charged a former deputy director for Caltrain and a former employee of TransAmerica Services with misusing public funds.

rows.title: Gen Z will spend $18,000 more on rent before they turn 30 than millennials did, study says
rows.standfirst: The youngest workers have the most to lose—and still no in-unit laundry.

rows.title: The Fed’s favorite inflation gauge slowed in February
rows.standfirst: The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% from January to February, decelerating from a 0.4% increase the previous month.

rows.title: The salary Americans need to buy a starter home has nearly doubled since the pandemic
rows.standfirst: “The pandemic housing market boom changed the definition of a starter home,” a Redfin senior economist said in a new analysis.

rows.title: The analyst who said greedflation was killing capitalism is rolling his eyes about AI: ‘Every bubble has a compelling narrative’
rows.standfirst: Albert Edwards of Société Générale also insists that AI isn’t driving markets—it’s loose monetary policy. And the recession still isn’t canceled.

rows.title: Walt Disney World dedicated nearly 80 acres to a massive affordable housing project near its Orlando park. But Orange County NIMBYs aren’t having it
rows.standfirst: “They’re trying to pack an enormous amount of density into what is essentially the size of a Costco parking lot,” resident said.

rows.title: Costco’s former CFO on ‘when, not if’ the $60 membership fee will go up: ‘It’s not some big analytical formula’
rows.standfirst: Former CFO Richard Galenti told analysts that Costco won’t just raise the price if sales fall off, and it will consider renewal rates and new sign-ups.

rows.title: Economists say you’re wrong for wanting prices to start falling—and they point to the Great Depression of the 1930s
rows.standfirst: “Most Americans are not just looking for disinflation,” the Fed’s Lisa Cook said last year. “They’re looking for deflation.”

rows.title: Jerome Powell doesn’t want to ‘jinx’ his war on inflation: ‘I’m a superstitious person’
rows.standfirst: Powell said Friday he still expected “inflation to come down on a sometimes bumpy path to 2%.”
